stability: Every entry in `outputs` is stable API: labels, basenames, and the field names/nesting shown in each example. Removing or renaming any of them is a breaking change and requires a TOOL_VERSION bump plus a changelog note here. Files NOT listed here are internal and may change or vanish without notice — in particular everything under ephemeral/ (face_tracks.json, identity_clusters.json, frame_index, detection_plan, cluster/search checkpoints), the media-processing run prefix the frames live under (MP's own service-derived prefix since 2026-09-18), and the bucket-root _facestore/ derivatives. Integrating against those paths is unsupported: a real consumer built its face overlay on ephemeral/face_tracks.json and ephemeral/identity_clusters.json instead of the face-groups / face-clusters entries below and broke silently when the intermediates changed. `description` is one line by design — it is joined verbatim into each get_job_status outputs[] entry as `desc`.

face-metadata.description: Screen-time/people summary — use for people lists, appearance timelines; montage via thumbnail_key, single reference face via rep_face_key
face-metadata.notes: people[] is sorted by total_screen_time_sec descending. name falls back to `Person_{person_id}` when named=false; name_source is `celebrity` | `collection` | `indexed` | null; face_id is the persistent-collection id when matched/indexed, else null; celebrity_id is the recognizer's celebrity identity key, gated in trust order: matched collection records carry a register-time celebrity_id, and EQUAL ids keep the key whatever the spelling while DIFFERENT ids (a collection homonym) suppress it; records predating the field fall back to case-insensitive name agreement between the published name and the validated vote's name (a collection witness that confirms the plurality keeps the key; a conflict resolved against the plurality suppresses it); else null; two people[] entries sharing a face_id or a celebrity_id are one person by the recognizer's own assertion — consumers may coalesce on it. celebrity_urls / known_gender (GetCelebrityInfo) accompany a set celebrity_id when the lookup succeeded, and are ABSENT — never null — when it was skipped or failed; known_gender is also absent when the lookup succeeded but Rekognition has no gender on record. get_celebrity_info_api in usage counts the (uncharged) GetCelebrityInfo lookups; it appears ONLY here, never in usage_tracking.json, which reports billed calls. appearances are merged track spans (minimum 800 ms), milliseconds from asset start; representative_frame is a source frame number. thumbnail_key and rep_face_key (like every *_key field) are S3 keys in the SAME bucket as this file, not s3:// uris — they point into the people-images prefix. thumbnail_key is the person's debug MONTAGE (contact sheet); rep_face_key is the single representative face crop (3:4 aspect, native resolution, ≤512 px long edge — the same face gender/age_range were read from). Use rep_face_key, never the montage, as a face-matching reference image. stats.cut_detector records which cut evidence bounded the tracks: `shots+dhash` (shot-segmentation supplement UNIONED with the built-in dHash veto — either detector's break splits a track) or `dhash` (built-in only). A person MAY additionally carry name_conflict: true plus name_conflict_detail {resolution, celebrity_name, celebrity_confidence, first_witness, second_witness} when the collection match disagreed with a validated celebrity plurality; the resolved name is still `name`/`name_source`, and the detail exists so the losing candidate is visible for audit — treat such a person's name as lower-confidence. usage counts Rekognition API calls only; full cost lives in the usage entry.

face-groups.description: Full per-face boxes/tracks — use for box overlays, frame-accurate face rendering
face-groups.notes: people[] entries repeat the face-metadata person fields and add tracks[]. box is frame-relative and normalized: l/t/w/h are 0-1 fractions of the ANALYZED frame's width/height (left, top, width, height) — multiply by the frame dimensions to get pixels. source is `detected` | `interpolated`: interpolated faces are synthesized for dedup-skipped frames by linear interpolation between the bracketing detections and carry ONLY frame_num/timestamp/box/gender/source (no frame_key, no attribute fields). centroid_idx indexes the track's representative face in faces[]. timestamp = frame_num / exact source fps, seconds from asset start. frame_key names a frame under media-processing's own run prefix — key faces by frame_num; do not integrate against that prefix. triaged_frames reasons: `black` | `mono` | `blur`. detection_plan.noisy_patches are 0-8 patch-grid indices (chronically-churning tickers/scoreboards) excluded from the skip test; skipped_gaps/dedup_skipped/dense_frames are counts.

face-clusters.description: 2D similarity coords per person — use for cluster/scatter visualizations
face-clusters.notes: Classical MDS embedding of the identity-similarity matrix (zero extra API calls). coord axes are unitless — only relative distances between people are meaningful. person_id/name/num_tracks/thumbnail_key join face-metadata's people[]. Written only when clustering produced similarity pairs; the outputs[] entry is omitted otherwise.

usage.description: Per-state cost, Rekognition API-call counts, media-processing child cost — use for reporting what this run cost
usage.notes: states is a dict keyed by state name (not a list). kind is `lambda` | `child_execution` | `task_token` | `map` — only lambda attempts are billed, so estimated_cost 0.0 on the other kinds is by design: the media-processing run's cost is reported as media_processing_cost (read from MP's published usage_tracking.json since 2026-09-18), and a task_token span is queue wait (semaphore) or the MP wait (held submit), and a map envelope's iterators are billed under their own names. Costs are us-east-1 arm64 estimates, not billing data.

people-images.description: Per-person images: montage JPEGs (avatars/UI lanes) and single representative face crops — face-metadata's thumbnail_key/rep_face_key are the per-person pointers
people-images.notes: Two files per person (zero-padded person_id): person_{NNNN}.jpg is the montage — up to 16 headshots evenly sampled across the person's full screen time; person_{NNNN}_face.jpg is the single representative face (3:4 aspect, native resolution, ≤512 px long edge — best track by appearance count, then that track's centroid face by area/frontality/sharpness). facemetadata.json's thumbnail_key and rep_face_key point at exactly these keys — prefer them over listing the prefix.

debug-grids.description: Detection/recognition grid JPEGs + raw Rekognition responses — human QC and audit, not a rendering input
debug-grids.notes: Mixed content: probe/dense detection grids ({item}_{grid}.jpg, with .a/.b recursive-split variants), celebrity grids (celeb_{item}_{batch}.jpg) each with the raw RecognizeCelebrities response beside it as {same}.jpg.json, and search_*.jpg persistent-collection query crops. Debug aid for human QC, not a rendering input.
